name: speed
note: The speed-up (keyboard.cpp, the SDK's app::SetSpeed), by a controller as SDL reads one (the virtual controller): the game at its own 60 frames a second (step.fps, the game's frames over the step's time), R3 clicked turns it to 2x (120: the pace doubled, one frame of each two shown, so the screen's refresh does not hold it back) and a fast-forward sign shows at the screen's top right, R3 again back to 60 and no sign; set to 4x, R3 runs it at 240 (above 150, for a slower machine) with the screen still at some 60 frames a second (telemetry speed.shown), and so with a heavy frame (400% render, ambient occlusion high, anti-aliasing): some 4 times the heavy frame's own rate at 1x, the screen at that rate (1.9.0 drew every frame: 4x came to the heavy frame's rate, the screen to a quarter of it); L3 with R3 opens the settings menu and leaves the speed as it is, R3 inside the menu does nothing; set off while on: back to 60, R3 does nothing. Ends at the game's own speed and the default setting (2x).

steps.note: 2x: the game's frames twice as many a second, the sign at the top right
R3: its own speed, for the heavy frame's own rate
a heavy frame (400% of the window's pixels, ambient occlusion high, anti-aliasing): the settle
the heavy frame at its own speed: as many frames as the graphics card draws, 60 at most

4x with the heavy frame: the frames let go draw nothing of the frame, so the game runs over 2.5 times the heavy frame's own rate (Windows on the RTX 3060: 230 a second against 60; Linux in WSL, whose frames cost more apart from drawing: 147 against 55) and the screen gets the heavy frame's own rate; in 1.9.0 every frame was drawn, 4x came to that rate, and the screen a quarter of it
both sticks: the settings menu, the speed as it was
R3 in the settings menu: nothing
both sticks again: the menu closed, the speed as it was
set off while on: its own speed
